preconditions.description: The number of split rules m and monster types n are at least 1.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= rule[0] <= n for rule in rules)
preconditions.description: Every split rule specifies a monster ID between 1 and n.

preconditions.expression: all(len(rule) >= 3 and rule[1] == len(rule) - 2 for rule in rules)
preconditions.description: Each rule line has a monster ID, a count li, and exactly li subsequent integers.

preconditions.expression: all(any(x == -1 for x in rule[2:]) for rule in rules)
preconditions.description: Every split rule produces at least one diamond (represented by -1).

preconditions.expression: all(any(rule[0] == i for rule in rules) for i in range(1, n + 1))
preconditions.description: Every monster type from 1 to n has at least one split rule.
The sum of li across all split rules is at most 10^5.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly n lines, one for each monster ID from 1 to n.

postconditions.expression: all(min_val == -1 and max_val == -1 for min_val, max_val in output_lines if not can_terminate_for_monster)
postconditions.description: If a monster cannot reach a state with zero monsters, both min and max are -1.

postconditions.expression: all(min_val == -1 and max_val == -2 for min_val, max_val in output_lines if can_terminate_for_monster and can_infinite_diamonds_for_monster)
postconditions.description: If a monster can terminate but can also produce an arbitrarily large number of diamonds, min is -1 and max is -2.

postconditions.expression: all(min_val == min_diamonds and max_val == max_diamonds for min_val, max_val in output_lines if can_terminate_for_monster and not can_infinite_diamonds_for_monster)
postconditions.description: If a monster can terminate and the diamond count is bounded, min and max are the smallest and largest possible diamond counts.

postconditions.expression: all(min_val <= 314000000 and max_val <= 314000000 for min_val, max_val in output_lines if min_val != -1 and max_val != -2)
postconditions.description: Any finite diamond count exceeding 314000000 is capped at 314000000 in the output.

postconditions.expression: all(min_val <= max_val for min_val, max_val in output_lines if min_val != -1 or max_val != -1)
postconditions.description: For any valid finite or infinite case, the minimum value is less than or equal to the maximum value.
